clue.text: Cruiser evacuated two islands in emergency

indicators.note: a word evacuated has had its insides emptied out, leaving only its two outer letters

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for island, here given twice

explanation.surface: A warship is cleared of its crew and sent between two islands during an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' leaves CR, the outside of Cruiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, a synonym for an emergency.

clue.text: Gave further consideration to how badly he got hurt

indicators.note: something done badly is botched or mangled, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone mulls over again just how severely a man was injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges HE GOT HURT; 'how' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think something over again, which is exactly giving it further consideration.

clue.text: Food that is rotten

parts.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning namely or that is
food that has gone bad is said to be off

explanation.surface: A plain remark about grub that has spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the scholarly abbreviation of scilicet, 'that is to say'. Scoff is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is informal British slang for grub or a meal, so it names food.

clue.text: Upset about family home robbed of contents in Barnet

indicators.note: the word for upset goes round the other pieces, so it is placed about them

parts.note: to be upset is to be sad
one's kin are one's family

indicators.note: a word robbed of its contents keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone distressed after relatives' house was burgled in Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but in rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair, so barnet is a hairstyle. 'robbed of contents' keeps HE from home; 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-shaven head is one particular hairstyle, and barnet is cockney rhyming slang for a person's hair.

clue.text: Hospital centre briefly treated deep cut

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed and changed, so they come out in a new arrangement
a word cut short briefly loses its final letter

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: At a hospital's main unit, a doctor quickly dealt with a serious gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims centre to CENTR, which 'treated' rearranges into TRENC before H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow excavation in the ground, a deep cut in the earth.

clue.text: Tax shelters stop being fashionable

indicators.note: the first word shelters, or holds within it, the second

parts.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it
to stop something is to end it

explanation.surface: Tax havens are no longer in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tax looks like a noun beside 'shelters', but it is the verb meaning to strain, TRY; 'being' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy follows the latest fashion, a direct synonym for fashionable.

clue.text: Appealed to men wanting leader dealt with

indicators.note: a word wanting its leader is missing its first letter

parts.note: a matter dealt with has been treated

explanation.surface: Requests were made to a group of men lacking a boss, and the issue was handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting leader' leaves EN from men.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly, so to have entreated someone is to have appealed to them.

clue.text: Store ready for those who listen

indicators.note: what reaches those who listen is the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: the ready, or readies, is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A shop is all set up for people who come to hear something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for those who listen' signals a word that sounds the same: the slang for money matches the hidden-hoard word in pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden stockpile of goods or supplies, so it is a store.

clue.text: Revolutionise banking system and National Insurance for a start

indicators.note: to revolutionise is to turn something completely round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: NI is the abbreviation for National Insurance, the British social security contribution
giro is a British system of bank transfers

explanation.surface: A call to overhaul the banks and the National Insurance scheme as an opening step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionise' turns NIGIRO, the two pieces together, end to end; 'for a' only joins. Giro is a British bank-transfer service; National Insurance is Britain's state contribution scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something begins, so it is a start.

clue.text: Give stick to someone facing something going rapidly downhill

definitions.meaning: in cricket, fielders taunt the batsman who is facing the bowling to unsettle him
a sled or toboggan that carries people quickly down snowy slopes

explanation.surface: Taunting an opponent while a toboggan careers down a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman 'facing' receives the ball, and sledging is the fielders' verbal abuse of him; to give stick is British for to criticise or mock.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb names cricketers' taunting of a batsman; the noun names a sled for sliding downhill.

clue.text: Speech having no boundaries or proportion

indicators.note: a word having no boundaries loses its first and last letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A talk that rambles on without limits or any sense of scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no boundaries' strips the outer letters of ORATION; 'or' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is what a proportion is.

clue.text: Author would endlessly seduce everyone alike

parts.note: the setter calls himself I, so the author would is I'D

indicators.note: each of the two words is used endlessly, losing its final letter

parts.note: to seduce is to entice
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A writer admits he would tempt every single person in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from both ENTICE and ALL, giving ENTIC and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly the same, so they are alike.

clue.text: Freak mistake by newspaper man including writer in document

parts.note: a goof is a blunder or mistake
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the writing tool sits in the legal paper, splitting it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A bizarre error from a journalist who slipped a writer into a document.
explanation.walkthrough: Freak looks like a noun but is the verb, to freak out; 'by' and 'including' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's temper or composure wildly is an idiom meaning to freak out.

clue.text: Patching frayed cover for the bedroom

indicators.note: something frayed has come apart at the edges, so these letters are unravelled and rewoven

explanation.surface: Mending a worn-out bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frayed' rearranges PATCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional soft hat worn in bed covers the head at night, so it is a cover for the bedroom.

clue.text: Nervously tiptoe, going rather hesitantly at first on this?

definitions.text: Nervously tiptoe, going rather hesitantly at first on this?

indicators.note: letters acting nervously jitter about into a new order
each of the three words is used for its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer creeps anxiously and haltingly along a high wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives GRH from going rather hesitantly, which 'Nervously' shuffles together with TIPTOE. The whole clue also describes a funambulist's walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut high wire is where a performer would edge along nervously and hesitantly, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Attack service in new set

indicators.note: the air force sits in the rearranged letters
new letters are a fresh arrangement of the old ones

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: An assault launched on a freshly assembled set of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives STE, with the air force placed 'in' it; the Royal Air Force is one of Britain's armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack repeatedly with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Broadcast word used to name church and houses

indicators.note: the first word houses, or contains, the rest

parts.note: a noun is the part of speech used to name a person, place or thing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A broadcast term used to identify a church and its buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word but supplies the outer letters that 'houses' wraps around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to make it public, which is what announced means.

clue.text: Abandoned taking action about disturbed rest

indicators.note: the word for an act goes about the other letters

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone gave up and acted because their sleep was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' gives SERT; 'taking' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted means left behind and forsaken, a synonym for abandoned.

clue.text: Name becomes label in complete senility

indicators.note: one letter becomes another piece, so it is swapped out

parts.note: a job that is complete is done
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A name turns into a mere label in total mental decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' looks like a verb but is just its abbreviation N; 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of weakened mental faculties in old age, so it means senility.

clue.text: Avoid going on motorway in small electric car

indicators.note: one piece goes on after the other, added to its end

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid
M is the abbreviation for a British motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the motorway in a tiny electric vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: M as in M1 or M25 labels a British motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a small electrically powered bumper car at a funfair.

clue.text: Enacted a reform giving PM opportunity to take steps

indicators.note: to reform letters is to reshape them into a new order

explanation.surface: A law is passed letting the Prime Minister take action.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister and steps like measures, but PM is afternoon and the steps are dance steps. 'reform' rearranges ENACTED A; 'giving' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon social dance held over tea is a chance, after midday, to dance.

clue.text: Finish tipping having blown raise

indicators.note: having blown something is having lost it, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: upending something is tipping it over
to up a price is to raise it

explanation.surface: A waiter ends up overturning things after losing out on a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having blown' removes UP from UPENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part of something, its finish.

clue.text: Take steps to get journey under way

indicators.note: in this down entry one piece sits under the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Taking action to get a trip started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts RIDE below ST in the down light; 'to get' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride is to walk with long steps, so to take steps.

clue.text: Completely covered in fluff from head to toe?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means thoroughly or perfectly, as in 'that suits me'

definitions.text: covered in fluff from head to toe?
definitions.meaning: soft fluffy feathers reaching all the way from the head to the floor

explanation.surface: Someone is entirely coated in fluff, top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: soft feathers stretching from head to floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means thoroughly or entirely; literally it pictures soft feathers that reach the floor.

clue.text: What author did with mind-numbing repetition

parts.note: learning by rote is learning through dull repetition

explanation.surface: A dig at a writer whose prose was tediously repetitive.
explanation.walkthrough: W for 'with' is a common abbreviation, as in w/.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors put words on paper, so what an author did was write; the past tense matches 'did'.

clue.text: Boy conducting detailed examination without parental guidance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are left out

parts.note: probing means investigating thoroughly
PG is the film certificate meaning parental guidance

explanation.surface: A lad being investigated closely while no parent is around to guide him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the P and the G from PROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is a boy's given name, and crosswords often take 'boy' to mean any male first name.

clue.text: Environmental expert first to pursue on-line carbon monoxide register

indicators.note: the ordinal comes after, pursuing the other pieces

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail, so online
CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide
a log is a register or record
1ST, first, is written with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A green specialist is the first to track online records of a poisonous gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pursue' places IST after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies organisms and their environment is an environmental expert.

clue.text: Food company breaking embargo

indicators.note: the firm breaks into the prohibition, splitting it

parts.note: an embargo is a ban

explanation.surface: A food firm defies a trade ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts CO into BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork from a pig's back or sides is a common food.

clue.text: Look up to one abandoning dream

indicators.note: the numeral is abandoning the daydream, so it is removed

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Admiring someone who gives up on a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes I out of REVERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to admire them deeply, an idiom-level synonym for looking up to them.

clue.text: Dreary tone returns in comic strip

indicators.note: the colour sits in the comedian's name

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comic

indicators.note: the colour word returns, read backwards

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour, a dreary tone

explanation.surface: A gloomy shade comes back in a cartoon strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic strip' looks like one phrase, but comic is Jack Dee, a deadpan British comedian, and strip is the definition. 'returns' gives NUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip something bare of its covering.
